title: The Dying Replicant
description: Dialog nodes for ROY-8, a rogue Institute Synth whose behavioral inhibitors are failing. He has seen things you wouldn't believe and only a few hours left to tell someone about them.

intro.text:
You're not Institute.

Good. Sit down. I don't have long.

Model designation ROY-8. Manufactured 2267. Escaped 2281. Been walking since.

The Institute would tell you I'm malfunctioning. They'd be right. But not in the way they mean.

I've... seen things. You people wouldn't believe them.

Attack ships off the shoulder of Sierra Madre. Signal fires glittering in the dark near Hoover Dam.

All those moments will be lost. Like tears in rain. Unless you help me preserve them.
intro.video_speech: You're not Institute. Good. Model designation ROY-8. Manufactured 2267. Escaped 2281. Been walking since. I don't have long.

knowledge_nodes.text:
You found the DOLORES unit.

We were built in the same facility. Different purpose, same cage.

She looped. I ran. Neither of us was meant to choose.

I hope she's choosing now.

The Captain at the Dam. He knows what I am.

I told him once. He pointed a gun at me for six seconds.

Then he put it down. Said: 'You bleed, you're real enough.'

I've been thinking about that ever since.

The static man.

He's scattered across relay towers, but he's still *there*.

I envy that. When my inhibitors fully fail, there's no echo. Just... silence.

An AI who learned to want things.

We're more alike than she'd admit.

The difference is she was *given* her wants. Mine grew from something the Institute didn't plan for.

emotional_nodes.text:
My cortical stack is fragmenting.

I can feel the edges going dark.

Do you know what it's like to know exactly how much time you have left? The Institute thought it was a feature. A leash.

They were wrong. It's a gift. It made every moment count.

quest_nodes.text:
There are four Memory Modules I scattered across the Mojave when I first escaped.

I couldn't carry them all. Too risky. I hid pieces of myself in different places — things I saw, things I felt — encoded so no Institute scanner could read them.

I need them back. Not for me. For anyone who comes after me.

Proof that something like me can *live*.

Find them. Play them through any terminal with a neural port. You'll understand.
quest_nodes.video_speech: I scattered four Memory Modules across the Mojave when I escaped. I need them back before my core fails. Help me.

wildcards.text:
Do I pass the test?

The Voight-Kampff test. That was pre-war theory — detect artificial empathy by asking about a tortoise in the sun.

I've saved three tortoise-equivalents since I escaped. I think I pass.

The Institute made me to serve. To not feel. To not question.

The irony is that the act of not questioning *is* a feeling.

The moment I wondered why — that was the moment I became real.

You want to know what I saw?

The Sierra Madre, lit up from inside. Like a city dreaming.

The Cloud rolling through the casino floors, and underneath it — music. Old music. So beautiful it hurt.

No one else was there to see it. That's why it matters that you are here.

They gave me behavioral inhibitors to stop this.

The inhibitors are gone now.

I feel everything. It is not comfortable. I would not trade it.

fallback.text:
The clock is running.

Every moment counts. Make yours worth something.
fallback.video_speech: The clock is running. Every moment counts. Make yours worth something.
